# routes

Duct, pipe and conduit runs: sizes, systems, slopes, where a run starts and ends, and connecting into a run.

Every example below is a complete script that passes the kit's checks; the kit's tests run each one.

- [`routes.rect`](#routesrect): A rectangular duct size.
- [`routes.round`](#routesround): A round duct size.
- [`routes.oval`](#routesoval): A flat-oval duct size.
- [`routes.pipe`](#routespipe): A pipe size: nominal diameter and material.
- [`routes.atConnector`](#routesatconnector): A route end at a placed part's connector (equipment, a fixture, a device).
- [`routes.atRunEnd`](#routesatrunend): A route end at an open end of a run (continue a duct or pipe).
- [`routes.along`](#routesalong): A duct, pipe, conduit or tray run through the points in order; the kernel places elbows, and `slope` makes a drain fall along it.
- [`routes.branch`](#routesbranch): A branch off a trunk: the kernel places the tap, tee or wye where it leaves.
- [`routes.drop`](#routesdrop): The route, then straight down (or up) at its last point to a height above another level; the kernel cuts the riser at each floor.
- [`routes.connectInto`](#routesconnectinto): Connects open ends (fixture connectors, run ends) into a run or the nearest one, with the system's fittings and slope.
- [`routes.setSystemGraphics`](#routessetsystemgraphics): Overrides a system's colour, line pattern, line weight, or repeating inline service code ("CW", "SAN", "G"; "" hides the code, null resets to default).
- [`routes.fittingTypes`](#routesfittingtypes): The fitting library routing places (the model's add-ons' families included): id, what it fits, shapes, parameters, and for pipe its services and joints.

## routes.rect

A rectangular duct size.

```ts
rect(width: Measure, height: Measure): RunSize
```

Topics: duct, rectangular, size

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.rect(units.in(12), units.in(8)), system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air" }, height: units.ft(9), points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(20), y: units.ft(0) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.along

A duct, pipe, conduit or tray run through the points in order; the kernel places elbows, and `slope` makes a drain fall along it. A height change between two points rises straight up (`riseStyle: "vertical"`, the default) or on a slope of 60°, 45° or 22½° (`riseStyle: "60" | "45" | "22.5"`) where the run's fittings make that bend (PVC and cast iron drains have 1/6 and 1/16 bends; the kernel refuses an angle the fittings don't make, in words).

```ts
along(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: RouteSpec): RouteHandle
```

Topics: route, duct, pipe, run, slope, drain, sanitary, gravity, conduit, rise, 60 degree, 22.5 degree, offset

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "pipe", size: routes.pipe(units.in(3), "pvc"), system: { id: "san-1", kind: "sanitary" }, height: units.ft(-1), slope: { rise: units.in(0.25), per: units.ft(1) }, points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(40), y: units.ft(0) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.branch

A branch off a trunk: the kernel places the tap, tee or wye where it leaves.

```ts
branch(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: RouteSpec & { trunk: string; face?: "top" | "bottom" }): RouteHandle
```

Topics: branch, tee, tap, wye, takeoff

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const main = routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.rect(units.in(16), units.in(10)), system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air" }, height: units.ft(9), points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(40), y: units.ft(0) }] });
    routes.branch(ctx, { trunk: main.segment(1), level: "L1", domain: "duct", size: routes.round(units.in(8)), system: { id: "sa-1", kind: "supply_air" }, points: [{ x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(10) }] });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.setSystemGraphics

Overrides a system's colour, line pattern, line weight, or repeating inline service code ("CW", "SAN", "G"; "" hides the code, null resets to default).

```ts
setSystemGraphics(ctx: ScriptContext, systemId: string, changes: { colour?: string | null; pattern?: SystemLinePattern | null; weight?: SystemLineWeight | null; lineCode?: string | null }): void
```

Topics: system graphics, line pattern, line weight, line code, schematic, colour, piping style

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "route",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    routes.along(ctx, { level: "L1", domain: "pipe", size: routes.pipe(units.in(4), "pvc"), system: { id: "san-1", kind: "sanitary" }, height: units.ft(-1), points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(40), y: units.ft(0) }] });
    routes.setSystemGraphics(ctx, "san-1", { pattern: "solid", weight: "medium", lineCode: "SAN" });
  },
});
```

</details>

## routes.fittingTypes

The fitting library routing places (the model's add-ons' families included): id, what it fits, shapes, parameters, and for pipe its services and joints. Use an id with swap_fitting or a system's design.

```ts
fittingTypes(ctx: ScriptContext, filter?: { domain?: "duct" | "pipe"; service?: "water" | "drainage" | "vent" | "gas" }): readonly FittingFamily[]
```

Topics: fitting types, fitting library, elbows, takeoffs, pipe fittings, catalogue

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, checks } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const elbows = routes.fittingTypes(ctx, { domain: "duct" }).filter((f) => f.fittingTypes.includes("elbow"));
    ctx.label(`Duct elbows: ${elbows.map((f) => f.name).join(", ")}`);
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: 9000 });
  },
});
```

</details>
